Hi Alicia / Paul — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

- Scope recap: POC to validate low-latency inference for batched customer events (50–200 req/s), strong data isolation (VPC+KMS), and cost projection for 3 months.
- Primary decision criteria you mentioned: latency SLOs, throughput on p3/rtx-class, security posture (SOC 2 / DPA), and total cost of ownership.
- Stakeholders I heard: Kunal (economic buyer), Alicia (security/compliance), Paul (procurement/ops). Please confirm any additions.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the economic buyer and the procurement contact who will own PO/terms? (Kunal + Paul in notes)
2) We’ll circulate a first-pass redline of the MSA and a sequencing recommendation (NDA already signed — correct?). Expect that in ~24 hours.
3) Procurement turn-time target? (e.g., 3–10 business days typical at your org)
4) Any mandatory clauses (IP, data residency, export controls) we should pre-seed?

Attached: Noventum_RFI_Summary.xlsx — short POC spec and test cases.

Proposed internal owners from our side: Rishi (sales owner / commercial), Neha (legal lead on redlines), Marissa (procurement coordination / billing). I’ve CC’d them.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the Draft MSA redline for review and a suggested routing order.

Best,

Thanks for the quick answers — below are concrete proposals so we can align expectations: 

Proposed routing & timing (our recommended order):
- 0: Security review (Alicia) — confirm SOC2, encryption, KMS requirements (1 business day to validate docs)
- 1: Commercial/MSA redline review (Neha) — first-pass redline sent to you (attached) and expected internal review 2–3 business days
- 2: DPA parallel track (once MSA terms are agreed in principal) — typically 1–2 business days for standard DPA
- 3: Procurement (Paul / Lara) — PO processing after legal sign-off (procurement turn-time you confirm; we assume 3–7 business days)

I’ve attached Draft_MSA_Redline_v1.docx — Neha will lead redlines. We can run the DPA in parallel to save time once we have MSA fundamentals agreed.

Security artifacts we can provide immediately: SOC2_Summary.pdf, data residency addendum, KMS integration notes. I’ll share the SOC2 link in a follow-up.

Next steps from us: Neha will circulate a tracked redline by EOD; Rishi will follow up with a 1‑page exec economic case for Kunal. Paul — can you confirm expected procurement SLA (Lara’s typical turn time) and whether Noventum requires vendor setup paperwork?

Thanks — cc’ing internal owners.

Best,
Soojin

Thanks all — quick legal note and estimated turnaround times so expectations are clear: 

- MSA: I’ve reviewed the deck and the draft MSA. I’ll return a tracked redline (Draft_MSA_Redline_v1.docx) within 3 business days for your internal review. If Noventum makes only limited comments we can close in 1–2 cycles; if there are material IP or indemnity changes expect additional time.
- DPA: We recommend running DPA drafting in parallel. Standard DPA edits returned in 1–2 business days.
- NDA: confirmed executed — no further action.
- Info we need from Noventum up front: SOC2 report snapshot, required data retention periods, and any specific export control language.

Routing recommendation:
1) Security confirms artifacts and any scope exclusions (Alicia) — 1 business day
2) Legal sends redline to Noventum (Neha) — 3 business days to first pass
3) Noventum legal/procurement responds to redline — target 3–5 business days
4) Finalize DPA in parallel once MSA terms agreed in principle
5) Procurement (PO) completes — dependent on your SLA (Paul / Lara)

Please send SOC2 snapshot and vendor setup form if there is one. Also note: for customers requiring HSM-backed KMS or custom data residency clauses, turnaround extends (usually +3–5 business days).

I’ve attached the MSA redline starter. I’ll track comments in the document and flag any commercial terms that need Soojin/Rishi input.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
